title: Correct and validate Chess Learning Assistant example moves

requirements.summary: Correct all learning example step data so every transition is a legal move and step board/move/lastMove are consistent (including Scholar’s Mate).
acceptanceCriteria: In the Learning view, each example can be stepped through from beginning to end without any step depicting an illegal move for the piece moved in that step.
For every step that includes lastMove, the piece shown on the board actually moved from lastMove.from to lastMove.to compared to the previous step, with any captured piece removed correctly.
The “Scholar's Mate (Basic Checkmate)” sequence is corrected so that bishop/queen/knight moves follow standard chess movement rules and match the shown board positions.
All user-facing descriptions and move strings remain in English and continue to describe the corrected positions accurately.

file_operations.description: Fully re-audit every example step and update positions/lastMove/move strings so each transition is legal and consistent. Explicitly fix the “Scholar's Mate (Basic Checkmate)” example so the bishop goes from f1 to c4 (not f3), the queen goes from d1 to h5, the black knight goes from b8 to c6, and the final capture Qxf7# reflects the correct capture/removals and lastMove coordinates across steps; ensure all descriptions remain accurate English.

requirements.summary: Add development-time runtime validation for learning examples and show a clear English error message in the Learning UI when invalid data is detected.
acceptanceCriteria: If an example contains invalid step data, the Learning view shows a clear English message indicating the example is invalid and should not render misleading steps.
If all examples are valid, the Learning view behaves exactly as before (no new warnings, normal rendering and stepping).
Validation does not require editing any immutable frontend paths (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts).

file_operations.description: Implement lightweight example validation utilities that compare each step to the previous step and detect: lastMove mismatching the board diff, illegal movement for the moved piece (pawn/knight/bishop/rook/queen/king, including castling and en passant patterns used by existing examples), invalid board shapes, and basic move-string/coordinate inconsistencies where feasible; return a clear English error list per example.

Run the example validator in development (e.g., gated by the build’s dev flag) when the Learning view loads and when changing examples; if the selected example is invalid, render a clear English error message and do not render the MoveStepper/Chessboard for that example to avoid showing misleading steps; if valid, preserve the current UI/behavior.
